=== Rutersju Hook ===

Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.
   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:

7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.

The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.

7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.
   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.
   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:

7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

[user]
=== Rutersju Hook ===

Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.

=== Rutersju Hook ===

Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.

   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.
   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Rutersju Hook uses a 36-card pack: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in clubs, hearts, spades and diamonds. Every player starts with 0 points. The game lasts 3 deals per player (0 deals at this table). The priority seat is seat 1 in deal 1 and moves one seat to the left (the next seat number, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1) after each deal.

CARD STRENGTH. Every card is written 'strength:card', and its strength runs from 1 to 36. The higher strength always wins. The 7 of diamonds is strongest (36), then the other diamonds A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 6 (35 down to 28), then the plain suits: aces (spade 27, heart 26, club 25), kings, queens, jacks, 10s, 9s, 8s, 7s and 6s, spades above hearts above clubs within each rank, down to the 6 of clubs (1).

EACH DEAL.
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and each player is dealt 3 cards face down. Each hand is seen only by its owner. Undealt cards stay hidden for the whole deal.
2. Bid (in turn). Starting with the player to the left of the priority seat and going left, each player in turn bids 0 to 3, hearing all earlier bids. The priority seat bids last.
3. The hook. The last bidder (the priority seat) may not choose a bid that makes the sum of all bids exactly 3: if the others' bids sum to s of 3 or less, the bid 3 - s is not offered. When the others' sum is already above 3, every bid is allowed.
4. Declarer. The player with the highest bid is the declarer. If several players tie for the highest bid, the one among them who bid last is the declarer. If every bid is 0, there is no declarer. All bids and the declarer are announced.
5. Tricks. Play 3 tricks. In each trick every player secretly and simultaneously chooses one card from their hand. All chosen cards are revealed together. The card with the highest strength wins the trick, and its player adds 1 to their trick count. There is no need to follow suit. Played cards stay face up and public.
6. Settlement, for each player separately, where d = |bid - tricks won|:
   a. If d = 0, the player gains 3 + bid points (bid 0: 3, bid 1: 4, bid 2: 5, bid 3: 6).
   b. If d > 0, the player loses 2 x d points.
   c. The declarer, if there is one, additionally gains 1 point if their d = 0, or loses 1 point if their d > 0. A player who is not the declarer gets neither.
   Because exactly 3 tricks are won and the bids never total 3, at least one player misses every deal.
7. All bids, trick counts and point totals are announced, and the priority seat moves one place to the left.

There is no discussion phase: players communicate only through their bids, which are public and made in turn, and through the cards they play. Scores may go negative.

END. After the last deal, the player with the highest point total wins. If two or more players tie for the highest total, it is a draw, shared among the tied players.
